div.head: Leis Wl 37.1
div.ab: E si de ço me mesc[re]ez, que pur pour de mort nel feisse, de ço m’esp[u]rj[e]rai.
E si de ço me mesc[re]ez que pur pour de mort nel feisse, de ço m'esp[u]rj[e]rai.
37, 1. Und wenn ihr mich dessen, dass ich es nicht aus Todesfurcht gethan habe, verdächtigt, werde ich mich davon reinigen’.
37, 1. And if you suspect me of not having done it for fear of death, I will clear myself of it’.
And if you suspect me of acting otherwise than through fear of death, I shall clear myself of the charge.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 268–269 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 515, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

mescez [instead of mesc'ez] Io; viescez Im, which earlier editors derive from vexare; MA. alters to vieltez (revile); suschez (suspect) Suchier Litbl. f. Germ. Phil. 1901, 121. Technically restez (rebuke, accuse) would also fit

Die Emendation gehört Fr. Michel bei Thorpe.—Offenbar kann die Reinigung deshalb nicht sofort erfolgen, weil Eideshilfe vorbereitet werden muss (diese fordern auch Jugements d’Oléron 8; vgl. künftig Seerecht von O. ed. Zeller), vermutlich Gefährdeeid; s. d. Gl. Ihr geht formale Klage voraus

The emendation is Fr. Michel’s, in Thorpe.—Evidently the purgation cannot take place at once because oath-helpers must be got ready (these are also required by the Jugements d’Oléron 8; cf. the forthcoming Seerecht von O. ed. Zeller), presumably for an oath of good faith; see that word in Gl. It is preceded by a formal charge
